manual.text:
## Specific task description

Task instruction: Pour the trash from the cup into the red box.

Task description: Pour the white paper-ball trash in the transparent cup on the table into the open red box to its left, emptying the cup.

Success criteria: The clear cup is picked up and emptied, with all trash originally inside falling into the red box and no trash remaining in the cup.

## Execution tips

- Consider gripping a rim-wall section near the robot hand with no waste obstructing the interior, one finger inside and one outside. Contact the wall with the pads and adjust the opening to local clearance, avoiding spanning the whole cup without an effective grasp.
- Clear cup walls can be hard to locate. Before closing, use both views to confirm the wall lies between the fingers. After gentle closure, lift slightly and check for slipping or deformation to avoid empty grasps or crushing the cup.
- The red box has high sides. During transport and tilting, leave enough clearance over the rim for the cup bottom, body, and gripper's rotation. Keep the lower side of the cup mouth above the inside of the opening during pouring to avoid rim collisions or dumping trash outside.
- Increase tilt slowly during pouring. If paper balls remain in the cup, rock gently while its mouth faces inside the box and rotation clearance permits. Check the bottom and walls for residue, avoiding abrupt swings that send trash flying outside.

narration: I will use the piper-control skill for this authorized real-robot episode strictly with the given parameters, following the manual and live observations returned by the tool.

I have read the manual and confirmed that only the right arm may be used. The paper ball inside the clear cup and open red box to its left are visible. I am adjusting the approach angle to grasp the rim and will first verify the grasp with a small lift.

The gripper is above the cup opening, and the cup remains securely on the table. I will continue reducing the step size and use both views to confirm that the cup wall is between the pads before closing.
The gripper has started closing, but the actual opening has not reached the set value yet. I will wait and check the contact state, then make a small test lift.

The cup stayed on the table during the first small lift, so an effective grasp has not formed. I opened the gripper and will lower the grasp position slightly within the same episode, then check again.
After regrasping, the actual opening stabilized around 6.6 mm and the cup followed a small lift. I will continue checking for slipping, then raise it enough to clear the red box rim.
The cup has left the table, the paper ball remains inside, and the grasp is stable. Next I will first increase the height to clear the box rim, then move the cup opening above the red box.

The cup has cleared the red box edge and is moving above the inside of its opening. There were already some paper scraps inside the box, so I will judge the pour based on changes to the paper ball inside the cup and the observed release.
Tilting has started in stages, and the grasp remains stable; the paper ball is still inside the cup. I will gradually increase the angle and pause to observe once the ball begins to slide.
Most of the paper balls have been observed sliding out through the cup opening, but a small piece is still visible inside. I will increase the tilt slightly and pause to check whether it empties.

No remaining paper ball was visible inside the cup in the last two observations, and the pickup and pouring motions are complete. I will end this episode. The cup is still held; the on-site operator will confirm whether all trash entered the red box.
